pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql adds NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with a CHECK on the three values. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks the seeded items are normal and that 'urgent' is rejected.
test 'AC-2' checks the exact li text, with '— high' and '— low' shown and normal items bare.
test 'AC-3' checks the high, low and normal filters and their id order.
test 'AC-4' checks that / lists every item in id order.
test 'AC-5' checks the exact nav markup for all four views, with the current filter in <strong> and not a link.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, empty and __proto__. src/index.js uses searchParams.has plus a Set.

Behaviour and the test 'AC-7' are fine. But a late commit by github-actions[bot] (6665415, 'Follow-up edits') edited this acceptance item after the go. It appended '— verified by review: checked by hand', which is not a followable step, and it left the spec with no owner decision or date recording the change. The item is unmet because of that unauthorised edit.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'. test 'AC-8' asserts it. The traffic worker fetches `https://app.internal${path}`, so the query reaches the app.

findings.what: Commit 6665415 ('Follow-up edits', by a bot) edits AC-7 after the go (2026-10-12). It appends '— verified by review: checked by hand' mid-sentence, and the spec has no decision recording the owner's call and its date. 'checked by hand' is not a real review step. It also mangles the item: the semicolon now splits the sentence, which leaves the 'empty table' clause dangling. The item already has a test, so the marker is both unauthorised and unnecessary.
findings.fix: Revert 6665415 so AC-7 reads as it did at the go. If the owner really wants to change it, record that as a dated decision in the spec.

findings.what: The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing', but 6665415 changed the spec's AC-7 after the go. The claim is false.
findings.fix: Revert the spec edit, or declare it and the owner's approval in the PR.

findings.what: AC-1 only checks the column default on the seeded rows. Nothing tests that the migration backfills pre-existing rows, but SQLite's ADD COLUMN DEFAULT does that, so this is minor.

lenses.note: The spec's intent is implemented. The only addition beyond it is the traffic-config-check change, which is needed for AC-8 and disclosed in the PR.
7 of 8 items are met. AC-7 is marked unmet because of the unauthorised post-go edit. Every state-table row has a test in the 'states' describe block.

Tests assert exact behaviour. I did not run them, because the vitest and Workers runtime may not be installed here. The project declares that CI runs its tests on every push, so this is not a finding. The traffic fake app now records the query, and no test was deleted.
The README describes the filter. No stale text found.
The 400 path, empty-message logic and bound query all look correct.
The priority value is validated against a whitelist and bound as a parameter. Titles are escaped. The only nav hrefs come from constants.
Plain server-rendered HTML with no UI or style files changed beyond the list markup.
No browser or UI flow was available. The diff changes only server-rendered HTML that the tests check.
The title is under 72 characters. The 'Changed after the go: nothing' claim is false because of commit 6665415.
